title: Classifying spaces of finite monoids with bounded homology
subject: math.AT
abstract: The classifying space BM of a monoid M is the geometric realization of the nerve of M, regarded as a category with one object; its fundamental group is the universal group U(M), the group generated by the elements of M with the multiplication table of M as relations. Let M be finite. We prove that if the integral homology of BM vanishes in all large degrees, then U(M) is trivial; more precisely, if a prime p divides the order of U(M), then H_k(BM; F_p) ≠ 0 for infinitely many k. It follows that three conditions on a finite monoid are equivalent: BM is homotopy equivalent to a finite CW complex; it is homotopy equivalent to a finite-dimensional one; its homology is bounded. In that case BM is simply connected. Together with a theorem of Ben-Bassat, that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to BM for a finite monoid M, this determines these homotopy types: they are the finite simply connected complexes. A conjecture of the same paper, that every connected finite CW complex with finite fundamental group is of the form BM with M finite, is therefore false; the real projective plane is a counterexample. The proof compares the K-theory of BM with that of the classifying space of a finite group contained in M, through Atiyah's completion theorem. Two examples are worked out: a monoid with six elements whose classifying space is simply connected and has homology in every degree from 2 on (it is a wedge of spheres), and a monoid with 23 elements whose classifying space is the complex projective plane.
comments:
Theorem 1.1: if the homology of a finite monoid M is bounded, its universal group U(M) is trivial; if a prime p divides |U(M)|, then H_k(BM; F_p) is non-zero for infinitely many k. Theorem 1.2: BM is homotopy equivalent to a finite complex if and only if to a finite-dimensional one, if and only if its homology is bounded. With Ben-Bassat's Theorem C, the spaces BM of finite monoids with bounded homology are exactly the finite simply connected complexes, and Conjecture 7.1 of arXiv:2610.38760v1 is false (the real projective plane is a counterexample). The proof compares the K-theory of BM with that of BG for the finite group G = eMe of the minimal ideal, through Atiyah's completion theorem. Examples: a six-element monoid with trivial universal group whose classifying space is a wedge of spheres of every dimension at least 2, and a 23-element monoid whose classifying space is the complex projective plane.

Checks: the main theorems were derived independently by Claude (Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5) and by GPT-6 Astra; the examples were recomputed by independent programs in exact integer arithmetic. No human has checked it; nothing is formalized. Records: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/mathematics-workbenches
